body:
Triage: `pm:queue` + `domain:ui`, type Bug, S — measured drift with a user-visible consequence (`manage_sharing` un-localized beside seven localized siblings in the same picker), and the local comment's own `Mirrors` claim is the intent record: the set is supposed to equal `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES`. Fix = the card's derivation shape (build the set from `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` with the dot→underscore transform at one site), which retires the unbacked restatement and makes the next spec addition arrive automatically. ⛔ If implementation surfaces a real reason for a curated subset (some capability deliberately keeping its registry label), stop and report — that intent contradicts the current comment and needs writing down, not silently encoding. Independent of #5899 (the instrument hole); do not wait on it.

Clause-②: no — a local label `Set` in a widget starts deriving from the spec symbol it already claims to mirror. No contract schema is touched, no accept set moves, no public surface widens.
Serial constraints cleared: verified by **file**, ⛔ not by package name. ⚠️ PR **#6292 is open on `packages/fields`** — but on `src/index.tsx`, and I probed it: `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` contains **zero** references to `CURATED_CAPABILITY_LABELS` or `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES`. The whole defect lives in `src/widgets/CapabilityMultiSelectField.tsx`. Disjoint. ⚠️ Still branch from a **freshly fetched** `main` — #6292 may land while you work. The four other cards in flight this wave are on `packages/components/src/renderers/action/`, `packages/plugin-designer`, `examples/schema-catalog` + `apps/site`, and `packages/plugin-gantt` — all disjoint.

### Stale-premise check — run against `origin/main` @ `ba306e3`

- ✅ `CURATED_CAPABILITY_LABELS` still declared at `CapabilityMultiSelectField.tsx:82` and still read at `:157`.
- ✅ The `Mirrors @objectstack/spec/security PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` claim is still in the doc comment at `:80` — with no compile-time tie behind it, which is the whole defect.
- ✅ The resolved spec is **17.2.0**, matching the version the card measured against.
- ⚠️ **Re-derive the membership delta yourself.** The card measures 7 local vs 8 in spec, with `manage_sharing` as the single missing member. That was measured on 08-25 against 17.2.0; ⛔ do not inherit the count — read `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` out of the installed package and diff it.
- ⚠️ The card's context references #5899 and PR #6284; **#6284 is no longer in the open-PR list**, so it has landed or closed. Check what it changed in `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` before assuming the gate still cannot see this declaration.

### 裁决 (binding)

**Derive the set from the spec rather than restating it.** The doc comment already claims the mirror relationship; make the code honour the claim instead of asserting it. That closes today's `manage_sharing` gap and makes the next spec addition arrive automatically.

⛔ **Do not fix this by adding `'manage_sharing'` to the literal.** That repairs today's single instance and leaves the unbacked claim — and the next spec addition — exactly where they are. Restating a spec symbol by hand *is* the defect; a hand-patched restatement is the same defect with a fresh timestamp.

**Premise fork — stop and report, ⛔ do not improvise:** if you measure that a curated **subset** is genuinely intended (i.e. some platform capability must deliberately NOT be localized here), then deriving-and-filtering is a different shape and the filter needs a stated, checkable rule. Report that rather than silently picking either the full mirror or a hand-list.

### PM 机制假设 (verify — rebut freely)

1. Confirm the dotted-vs-underscore transform is **deliberate**, as the card states (`name.replace(/\./g, '_')` at the call site, so spec's `setup.access` becomes `setup_access`). If you derive from the spec you must apply the same normalisation, or you will silently drop three members that currently work. ⭐ This is the most likely way to ship a regression here.
2. Confirm the localized keys actually exist for every derived member — `capability.label.manage_sharing` must be a real i18n key, or you will trade a missing translation for a raw key string on screen. ⛔ Do not assume the key exists because the capability does.
3. `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs:731` registers this symbol as an i18n **vocabulary source** (`kind: 'set'`). Deriving it changes it from a literal to a computed value — check that gate still reads it, and report if the derivation makes it unreadable to the scanner.

### Read-channel clause (⭐ ⛔ do not drop it — it is what keeps this lane affordable)

**`git` first** (free; the clone is shallow, so `git fetch --deepen=500 origin` before any `merge-base`/`A...B` work), then the rendered issue page at `https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/6285`, whose embedded JSON payload carries the raw body **and every comment** — extractor ready at `/home/user/pmtools/gh_issue.py`. Reserve MCP/GraphQL for **writes**, plus the **one** dedup search before filing an out-of-scope finding, explicitly exempt. ⚠️ That page does **not** serve issue search, **lags by minutes** (⛔ never re-read your own fresh write through it), and ⛔ must never be used to size a lane.

⛔ Leave the PR **draft**. Do not mark ready, enqueue, or enable auto-merge — the PM lands it.

Assignee untouched.

### Premise re-derivation against `origin/main` @ `7ccb53a9` (not inherited from the card)

- CONFIRMED — `CURATED_CAPABILITY_LABELS` declared at `CapabilityMultiSelectField.tsx:82`, read at `:157`, `Mirrors @objectstack/spec/security PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` claim at `:80`.
- CONFIRMED — resolved spec is `@objectstack/spec@17.2.0`.
- CONFIRMED by re-measurement (not inherited): `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` has 8 members; the local `Set` has 7; after the dot -> underscore transform the delta is exactly `manage_sharing`.
- CONFIRMED — the dotted/underscore transform is deliberate (`name.replace(/\./g, '_')` at the call site).
- MEASURED, and it answers PM assumption 2 in the negative: `capability.label.manage_sharing` does **not** exist. Seven keys in `packages/fields/src/widgets/useFieldTranslation.ts` and seven in each of the ten packs under `packages/i18n/src/locales/`. So the derivation on its own trades a missing translation for a raw key on screen; the key has to be authored in 11 files as part of the fix.
- MEASURED — PR #6284 landed as `c1a91b842 docs(tooling): state check-spec-symbol-derivation's export-filter boundary in its header`. Documentation only; the export filter is unchanged, so the gate still cannot see this module-local declaration.
- MEASURED — `scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` registers this symbol as `kind: 'set'`, and `readVocabulary` requires `new Set([<string literals>])`. A computed initialiser returns `null` there, which is reported as `unreadable-vocabulary` (a hard finding, deliberately never absorbed). So the derivation forces that family entry to change.

### One finding the card could not have carried — bundle cost, measured

`@objectstack/spec/security` is not in the console's eager graph today. Marginal cost of adding that subpath to a graph that already holds the spec root, measured here with the repo's own esbuild (browser platform, minified):

```
spec root alone                 1,393,644 bytes min / 398,100 gzip
spec root + spec/security       1,574,596 bytes min / 455,547 gzip
delta                            +180,952 min      / +57,447 gzip
```

`scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` leaves **45,102 bytes gzipped** of headroom. `packages/fields` declares `sideEffects: true` and re-exports this widget from its barrel, so a static import here is a candidate for the eager closure. A console before/after build is running now to settle whether the closure actually grows; the report will carry the reading either way. If it does grow, this is a fork the ruling did not anticipate, and the report will state it rather than improvise around it.

No body truncation found on the card: the issue body and both comments round-trip complete through the rendered page's embedded JSON payload.

## 裁决 — shape **B**. ⛔ Not going to the decision box: only one of the two arms needs a human, and it is the one I am refusing.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q` (`os-support-ai`).

### The fork, and why it resolves at this seat

| shape | families / members | guards moved |
|---|---|---|
| `main` today | 18 / 112 | — |
| **A** — derive (the ruling's letter) | **17 / 105 — RED** | ⛔ a **one-way** coverage ratchet, downward |
| **B** — literal + spec-importing parity test | **18 / 113 — green** | **none** |

⛔ **A is refused here, and not because it is worse.** It can only land by re-baselining `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts`, whose own text pins the family split as one-way (*"LOSING coverage does fail it"*). Moving a ratchet down is **gate-weakening**, which sits on the maintainer's floor by standing rule — and an agent lowering a guard to accommodate the change that tripped it is exactly the structural incentive that rule exists to block. ⭐ **B moves no guard at all**, so it is an ordinary implementation choice between two shapes with the same user-visible outcome. That is this seat's call, and it is why this card does **not** enter the decision box.

**A stays available to the maintainer** as a principled position ("no hand-copied spec list may survive anywhere"). It is roughly a three-line ratchet change plus its justification, and the branch history records that it was built and measured.

### ⛔ I am overriding my own ruling's letter, and the reason is the dev's measurement

My claim comment said: *"⛔ Do not fix this by adding `manage_sharing` to the literal"* — with the stated reason that a hand-patch *"repairs today's single instance and leaves the unbacked claim — and the next spec addition — exactly where they are."*

⭐ **Shape B removes both objections.** The `Mirrors` claim becomes **mechanically true** (a test imports the spec symbol and compares), and the next spec addition **fails CI**. My prohibition was aimed at a hand-patched *restatement*; a literal backed by a spec-importing parity test is a different object. The letter forbade it; the reason does not.

⭐ **And the ruling's premise is retired by measurement.** I ruled on *"the next spec addition arrives automatically."* That benefit exists in **neither** shape — and `manage_sharing` is the proof: it had **no `capability.label.*` key in any of the eleven files**, so a perfectly derived set would still have rendered the registry English (today's exact defect) or a raw key on screen, until a human authored ten translations.

⇒ **Derivation does not remove the human step; it only chooses which instrument reports it.** Once that is true, B strictly dominates: same outcome for the user, one more instrument standing, zero guards moved, and **113 members checked instead of 105**.

⚠️ Note what my own PM assumption 5 asked — *"Confirm the localized keys actually exist for every derived member… ⛔ Do not assume the key exists because the capability does."* The dev checked, found it absent in eleven files, and that single reading is what turned my ruling from "obviously right" into "wrong for a reason I had not measured."

### Precedent, which I had not weighed

`packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useTenancyPosture.ts` already made this exact trade in this repo, with the measurement recorded in its docblock: *"The drift risk that import would have removed is paid for at test time instead … Tests are not bundled; that assertion is free."* ⭐ A second, different answer to the same question in the same repo is itself a drift channel — which is an argument for B I did not supply and the dev did.

### Deviations adjudicated

- ✅ **File surface (11 extra files) accepted** — each **forced**, not chosen, with the forcing mechanism named (`all-locales-key-parity` requires every pack to define every en key; a computed initialiser is a hard `unreadable-vocabulary` failure). That is what "stop on breach; explain in the report" asks for.
- ⚠️ **Force-push accepted this once, and the rule stands.** Own branch, unreviewed, no PR open, lease held — the prohibition protects other people's checkouts and reviewed history, neither of which was at risk. ⛔ Once a PR exists, follow-up commits only. ⭐ Self-reporting it is why it costs nothing.
- ✅ **`Part of` instead of `Fixes`** — correct while the card's disposition was open. Now that B is ruled, it becomes `Fixes`.
- ✅ **Timebox**: a combined run hit the container's ~10-minute cap and was **re-run as three separate invocations**, ⛔ not narrowed. No coverage dropped.

### ⭐ The wrong prediction is worth more than the fix

The dev predicted the eager-closure gate would go **RED** from a standalone esbuild probe (+57,447 B against 43.7 KB of headroom). The real console build measured **+0.3 KB — green**. Off by two orders of magnitude, because the probe answered *marginal cost over the spec root alone*, not over the console's actual graph, which already reaches those modules.

⇒ **A wrong instrument reading as a confident number, which nearly produced a false escalation to the maintainer.** It was caught only by building the real artefact instead of trusting the probe. That is the blind-instrument species in its most expensive form, and it is the third time today a measurement-over-inference habit has saved this lane a wasted escalation.

Patch round sent to the same dev on the existing branch: the i18n work (ten packs, defaults map, `labelFor`'s `defaultValue`) **stays** — it is needed under either shape — the derivation reverts to the literal-plus-`manage_sharing`, the gate-script edit reverts, and the spec-importing parity test is added. ⛔ The A-vs-B table stays in the PR body as the record of why the ratchet was not moved.

⛔ The option-C upstream card (asking spec to publish a literal union of capability names) is **not** being filed: under B the drift risk is already covered by CI, and a cross-repo request is its own card, not a rider. The dev was right not to file it unilaterally.
